description: Composable, accessible components with thoughtful defaults. Build your own component library with code you can customize, extend, and make your own.

summary.one_liner: shadcn/ui is an open-source collection of copy-in React/Tailwind-style UI components that you add to your own project and customize, rather than installing as a locked dependency.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a set of beautifully designed components that users can customize, extend, and build on, positioned as a starting point for building your own component library. It is open source with open code, so the component source lives in your project rather than behind a package boundary. The README itself is brief and points to external documentation for installation and component details, and to a contributing guide. The GitHub topics indicate support for React, Next.js, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Radix UI, React Aria, Base UI, TanStack, and Laravel, though the README does not spell out these integrations in detail. The repository is MIT licensed.
use_cases: Build a custom React component library
Start a UI kit with accessible building blocks
Add prebuilt components to a Next.js or Vite app
Customize buttons, forms, and dialogs in a Tailwind project
Create a design system based on editable component source
notable: Open code: components are meant to be copied into your project and edited directly
Composable and accessible components with thoughtful defaults
Documentation hosted externally; README links only to it and a contributing guide
Topics show support for multiple underlying primitive libraries (Radix UI, React Aria, Base UI)
caveats: README is minimal and defers installation and usage details to external documentation
README does not name specific supported frameworks or platforms; those come from GitHub topics only
